passages.t: ‘No one cares for my soul’: a prayer from the cave
passages.happening:
The heading reads, “A Maskil of David, when he was in the cave. A prayer” (verse 1). “I cry aloud to the LORD; I lift my voice to the LORD for mercy” (verse 1). “I pour out my complaint before Him; I reveal my trouble to Him” (verse 2).

He is worn out. “Although my spirit grows faint within me, You know my way” (verse 3). Traps are hidden on his path (verse 3).

Then the loneliest line in the psalm. “Look to my right and see; no one attends to me. There is no refuge for me; no one cares for my soul” (verse 4).

But he turns to God. “I cry to You, O LORD: ‘You are my refuge, my portion in the land of the living’” (verse 5). “Listen to my cry, for I am brought quite low” (verse 6). “Free my soul from prison, that I may praise Your name” (verse 7). And he hopes for company again: “The righteous will gather around me because of Your goodness to me” (verse 7).
passages.hearers:
The heading sets the prayer in a cave. David hid in caves more than once while Saul hunted him. At the cave of Adullam, “all who were distressed or indebted or discontented rallied around him” (1 Samuel 22:2). Later, in a cave in the wilderness of En-gedi, he spared Saul's life (1 Samuel 24). The heading does not say which cave. Psalm 57 has a heading like it. The book page explains these headings.

‘Look to my right’ (verse 4) would make sense to a first hearer. In a court or in battle, a friend or defender stood at your right hand. The singer looks there and sees no one.

‘My portion’ (verse 5) is a word from the sharing out of land. Each family had its portion. The singer has lost everything and everyone, and says that God himself is what he has.

A cave can feel like a prison (verse 7). The singer wants out, not only for his own sake, but so that he can praise God among others again.
passages.later:
Jesus knew this loneliness. On the night he was arrested, “all the disciples deserted Him and fled” (Matthew 26:56). He had told them, “you will leave Me all alone. Yet I am not alone, because the Father is with Me” (John 16:32).

Paul wrote near the end of his life, “At my first defense, no one stood with me, but everyone deserted me” (2 Timothy 4:16). And then: “But the Lord stood by me and strengthened me” (2 Timothy 4:17).
passages.hard: If ‘no one cares for my soul’ is how you feel, please hear this: the person who prayed this psalm felt it too, and God kept his prayer in the Bible. Loneliness is not a sign that God has forgotten you. Tell God, as this singer did. Then, if you can, tell one person: a pastor, a friend, a neighbour. If loneliness has become despair, or you have thoughts of hurting yourself, speak to someone today. The Find Help page on this site lists places to turn.
passages.asks:
Psalm 142 shows a man who poured out his complaint. He did not tidy it up. He said, ‘No one cares.’ You may pray that honestly too.

And look at the end. He hopes the righteous will gather around him again. Is there someone in your life who is in a cave right now, with no one at their right hand? You might be the one who stands there.
